name: agent-cortex token map
description: Central mapping of tool names, paths, and agent naming conventions across the claude and pi harnesses. Single source of truth for install-time token substitution. See token-map.README.md for the design rationale.

token_format.decision: Adopt the {{TOOL:name}} / {{PATH:name}} / {{SECTION:name}} grammar already standardised by ADR #63 (agents/README.md) rather than a dotted {{tool.name}} form. The uppercase type prefix disambiguates token kinds at a glance, keeps tool/path/section names in one namespace collision-free, and matches the token grammar skills are already written against.

types.TOOL: {{TOOL:<canonical tool key>}} — replaced at install time with the bound harness's tool name (see tools).
types.PATH: {{PATH:<path key or relative path>}} — replaced at install time with the harness-resolved path (see paths).
types.SECTION: {{SECTION:<name>}} — replaced by the agent composer with <harness>/<name>.md section content. Not a global substitution; out of scope for token-map.json (see contract).

sources.pi: agents/<name>/ composable dirs (canonical) — composed at runtime by the agent-modes extension
sources.claude: agents/<name>/ composable dirs (canonical) — composed by bin/installers/claude.mjs (install-time generator, the only generator — the generated claude/ plugin subtree is not committed)

wake.description: How each harness tells ralph that a background worker finished. `{{SECTION:wake}}` in agents/ralph/agent.md resolves to agents/ralph/<harness>/wake.md; this table is the machine-readable form of the same fact, so the mechanism is recorded rather than inferred from prose (see the wake table in agents/README.md).

notes.pi: Blocking wait: wait_for_agents returns as soon as one worker finishes, carrying its result inline. No timer to start, nothing to kill — there is no poll loop.
notes.claude: Event-driven: the harness re-invokes ralph when a worker completes and delivers the result inline. No poll timer, no sleep, no log flush.

tools.rg: Canonical alias for grep. Claude and pi collapse it onto their single search tool (Grep / grep).
tools.glob: Claude has a dedicated Glob tool. pi's built-in pattern-search tool is find (hypa_find when the pi-hypa extension is installed).
tools.ask_user: Claude (AskUserQuestion) prompts the user mid-run. pi's equivalent is ask_questions, provided by the pi-questions package (an ordinary runtime dependency of this package that `agent-cortex install pi` bundles into the staged package's node_modules) — the genuine interactive-questioning tool, restoring grilling in plan/ralph-plan/strategy modes. Like fetch_content (pi-web-access), it is only present when its package is installed, so the mapping depends on that package (see the extension-manifests idea). pi still intentionally ships no permission popups; ask_questions is the interactive mid-run question tool, not a popup.
tools.web_fetch: pi's fetch_content comes from the pi-web-access package (an ordinary runtime dependency of this package that `agent-cortex install pi` bundles into the staged package's node_modules).
tools.skill: Claude (Skill) exposes skills as a tool. pi has no dedicated skill tool — skills are surfaced in the always-present 'Available skills' context block and loaded by reading the listed SKILL.md path ({{PATH:<skill>/SKILL.md}}). The pi mapping is read, the tool used to load a skill's file; a dedicated skill tool is a follow-on design candidate if prompting proves insufficient.
tools.read_agent: Claude's Task returns results inline — there is no separate read step, so read_agent drops on claude (null). pi exposes read_agent as a fallback to wait_for_agents.
tools.task: Claude provides a subagent tool natively. On pi it is supplied by this repo's own extensions/subagent extension (which also registers read_agent and wait_for_agents), not by pi itself — a pi session started before that extension was installed has no dispatch tool at all. Skills must therefore stop and report a missing subagent tool rather than improvising a backgrounded CLI run, which has no completion signal.
tools.wait_for_agents: PI-only blocking wait over background subagent runs (the task tool): returns the results of completed agents and STILL RUNNING for the rest. Claude's Task delivers results inline with no wait step — null on claude.

paths.pi: plugin_root is the staged package `agent-cortex install pi` materialises at ~/.agent-cortex/pi; pi loads that directory by path and the shipped extensions resolve their own resources relative to it (agent-modes computes plugin_root from its actual install location). A checkout or symlinked install differs — installers compute plugin_root from the actual resolution and can override it (--plugin-root).
paths.claude: plugin_root stays ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (env var) for the materialised plugin — never a literal ~/.agent-cortex/claude. Claude Code copies marketplace-installed plugins (including local directory sources like ~/.agent-cortex/claude) into its own cache and expands the env var per context, so a literal home path in substituted files would break under cache-copy; the installer passes the env form through verbatim.

agents.prefix: Claude strips the agent-cortex: name prefix during conversion (NAME_PREFIX in bin/installers/claude.mjs): pi agents are agent-cortex:<slug>, claude agents are <slug>.

contract.summary: Installers substitute {{TOOL:...}}, {{PATH:...}}, and {{SECTION:...}} tokens in generated harness files using this map. This contract is the single reference installers must implement; token-map.json is the data those rules operate on.
contract.binding: The harness id is the same value the installer is invoked with (agent-cortex install <harness>). Each harness reads its own column from the tools, paths, and agents sections.
rules: TOOL: replace {{TOOL:<key>}} with tools.<key>.<harness>. Canonical keys are exact, case-sensitive strings (the names the canonical sources in agents/<name>/agent.md are authored with).

TOOL null: a null value means the harness has no equivalent. In prose, remove the token (and emit a warning). In a tool-list context (frontmatter tools: [...]), omit the entry. Do not substitute an empty string.

TOOL unknown: a {{TOOL:<key>}} with no entry in tools is a hard error — the map must be extended. This mirrors the generators (bin/installers/claude.mjs, bin/installers/pi.mjs), which throw on unknown tools.
PATH named key: replace {{PATH:<key>}} with the resolved value of paths.<key>.<harness>.

PATH resolution: a value may be a literal string, an ${ENV_VAR} token, or a {base, relative} spec. Resolve {base, relative} by joining relative onto the resolved base. Leave ${ENV_VAR} values verbatim — the harness expands them at runtime (claude's ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}).
PATH unknown base: a {base, relative} spec whose base is not a key in paths is a hard error.

SECTION: {{SECTION:<name>}} is resolved by the agent composer from <agents_dir>/<harness>/<name>.md; token-map.json does not substitute it. Installers must leave SECTION tokens untouched for the composer.
Contract version: installers must reject token-map.json versions higher than the contract version they implement.
Case sensitivity: all token arguments and map keys are case-sensitive.

error_handling.unknown_tool: throw — the map must stay complete
error_handling.unknown_path_base: throw — the map must stay complete
error_handling.null_tool_in_tool_list: omit the entry from the array
error_handling.unsupported_version: throw with the supported version range
